checks.label: The spread of a mean is the spread of one reading divided by the square root of the number of times the measurement was repeated: over 2,000 beads from the rule on screen, single readings spread 0.04 V, and means of 2 and of 4 readings spread 1 ÷ √2 and 1 ÷ 2 as widely, within 5%

Systematic: the same influence affects the result for each of the repeated measurements, so you learn nothing extra just by repeating. With the meter 0.01, 0.02 or 0.03 V high, every reading of the batch lands exactly that much higher, and so does the mean, whether each bead is the mean of 1, 2 or 4 readings; the scatter is unchanged

An accuracy of ±(2% + 2) means a reading of 100.0 V can be from 97.8 V to 102.2 V; by the same rule ±(1% + 3 digits) on 50.0 V read to 0.1 V gives 49.2 V to 50.8 V, as the rating puzzle draws it, and the example meter's ±(0.1% + 2 digits) at 27.00 V read to 0.01 V reaches 0.047 V either side, the width of the window behind the hopper

Worked by hand from this batch: one reading a bead gives a mean of 27.00 V, an SD close to 0.04 V and a result of ± 0.011 V (2 × 0.04 ÷ √50, with √50 about 7.07), with 49 of the 50 within 0.08 V of 27.00 V and one at 27.06 V; two a bead about seven tenths as wide; four a bead half as wide and ± 0.006 V; 0.02 V high and four a bead, 27.02 ± 0.006 V, missing 27.00 V; against 27.02 V the result sits below, below, across and above as the offset rises; on the 0.05 V meter every reading is a whole step and the mean moves under 0.002 V; 0.82 ± 0.03 Ω runs 0.79 to 0.85 Ω, across 0.84 Ω

Drawn right: settled, the fulcrum sits under the mean and the beam is level at every setting of averaging, offset and meter step; the hopper sits over 27.00 V plus the offset, inside the window; the limit line sits at 27.02 V; no bead is under r 3.5 or off the scale; no dashed line runs through a label

Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, and before an answer nothing in its picture gives it away: no reach round the ringed reading, no SD bracket, no spread of single readings, no rated range, no result after the switch to four, no bracket round 0.82 Ω, still the 0.05 V meter; a right answer brings each in. Every demonstration settles within 4.5 s and every answer's motion within 2.5 s
